description: Arrow Protocol Classification Binding Methods Registry. Controlled vocabulary for proof_semantics.classification_binding_method. Defines the mechanism by which source-domain output type classification is proven, attested, audited, or inferred. Referenced by SEM-017 and MSG-005.

schema_notes.max_confidence_ceiling: Maximum Confidence claimable by events using this classification binding method, absent stronger verification. Implementations MUST NOT allow events to claim Confidence above this ceiling when this method is declared.
schema_notes.requires_audit_ref: If true, events using this method at Confidence above C MUST provide classification_audit_ref in the Bridge Registry entry or event metadata.

entries.name: Native Protocol Type System
entries.description: Classification is enforced by the source chain's own type system, consensus rules, or state machine. The protocol itself guarantees the type of every output. No external verifier is required — the type is inherent to canonical state.
examples: Bitcoin transaction output type enforced by Script rules
Ethereum ERC-20 transfer enforced by token contract ABI
Verus PBaaS export type enforced by PBaaS consensus — source side only
entries.notes: This is the only method that can support Confidence A. If this method is declared, the source chain's own type system must be the authoritative classifier — not an external observer.

entries.name: Contract Verified
entries.description: The bridge or verification contract at the destination explicitly enforces that the proven object matches the claimed destination type. The contract's logic is the classification check — acceptance of the proof implies type validation by the contract code.
examples: Destination bridge contract validates that proven Merkle leaf is a transfer-type output
Smart contract enforces structural type constraints on accepted proofs
entries.notes: Requires classification_audit_ref pointing to contract code, formal verification report, or independent audit. The Verus-Ethereum Bridge exploit is the canonical failure of this method being absent — the contract accepted the proof without validating its type.

entries.name: Canonical Verifier
entries.description: An officially designated verifier — recognized by the source chain's governance or protocol specification — explicitly attests to the classification of the proven object. The verifier is part of the source chain's canonical infrastructure.
examples: Designated notarization nodes attesting to Verus PBaaS export type
Protocol-designated oracle attesting to output classification
entries.notes: Canonical verifier status must be documented in the Bridge Registry entry. Requires classification_audit_ref to the governance record or protocol specification that designates the verifier.

entries.name: Formal Verification
entries.description: The classification claim is backed by a machine-checked formal proof — e.g. a proof assistant (Coq, Lean, Isabelle) or formal methods verification — demonstrating that the bridge contract or verification circuit correctly classifies all inputs of the claimed type.
examples: Formally verified ZK circuit that proves output type membership
Coq proof that the bridge contract correctly enforces type constraints
entries.notes: The only non-native method that can support Confidence A. Requires classification_audit_ref to the publicly accessible formal verification artifact. Machine-checked means human-audited is insufficient for this method — the proof must be mechanically verifiable.

entries.name: Independent Audit
entries.description: A qualified independent security auditor or audit firm has reviewed and confirmed the classification binding mechanism. The audit report is publicly accessible. This is a one-time or periodic human review, not a continuous enforcement mechanism.
examples: Halborn, Trail of Bits, or equivalent firm audit confirming type enforcement logic
Third-party security review confirming that bridge contract validates output type
entries.notes: Audit results decay over time as code changes. A Bridge Registry entry relying on independent_audit must document the audit date and scope. Post-upgrade re-audit is required before confidence ceiling applies to the updated version.

entries.name: Governance Approved
entries.description: The classification binding mechanism has been reviewed and approved through a documented on-chain or off-chain governance process. The approval record is publicly accessible and links to a specific implementation version.
examples: DAO governance vote approving specific bridge contract version with type enforcement
Protocol foundation committee approval with public record
entries.notes: Governance approval is a process check, not a technical proof. It establishes accountability and reviewability but does not substitute for technical enforcement. Combined with contract_verified or independent_audit, it can support the full Confidence B ceiling.

entries.name: Context Inference
entries.description: Classification is inferred from surrounding context — e.g. transaction structure, protocol convention, or observed behavioral patterns — rather than explicitly proven, attested, or enforced by a verifier or contract. This is the weakest binding method and the reference failure case.
examples: Destination contract assumes output type from transaction position without explicit type proof
Bridge infers export type from calldata structure without enforcing it cryptographically
Verus-Ethereum Bridge at time of exploit — type inferred, not proven
entries.notes: This is the reference case. Context inference was the implicit method used by the Verus-Ethereum Bridge: the destination contract accepted a proof of data existence and inferred its classification from context. Events using context_inference MUST NOT claim Confidence A or B per SEM-017. SEM-017 caps context_inference events at Confidence C.

entries.name: None
entries.description: No classification binding mechanism is declared or available. The event does not attempt to prove, attest, or infer the source-domain classification of the proven object. Classification is absent. Use only when the event explicitly acknowledges this limitation in its proof_semantics block.
examples: Custodian attestation of a balance without cross-chain type claims
Legal instrument referencing an on-chain event by hash without classifying its output type
entries.notes: Events declaring method_id=none are capped at Confidence D. They are suitable for awareness, monitoring, or provisional state tracking. Not suitable for value-releasing or settlement-triggering actions.
